title: Update on Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme and Impact of Exit of Electricity Retailers on SMEs and Support Available
what_it_is: Update on Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme and Impact of Exit of Electricity Retailers on SMEs and Support Available

sections.label: Questions on TRECS and electricity retailers
sections.summary: Questions ask about TRECS take-up, unsupported companies, retailer exits, SME electricity bills, and extending TRECS beyond February 2022.

sentences.text: The following question stood in the name of Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui – 41 To ask the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) to date, what is the take-up rate of the Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme (TRECS); (b) what is the number of companies not supported by TRECS; (c) what is the cost delta impact on these companies and the reasons for not being supported; and (d) whether the Ministry intends for TRECS to continue for an extended period of time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the Ministry's assessment of the effect of the exit of various electricity retailers in 2021 on the electricity bills of small and medium enterprises (SMEs); and (b) how is the Government monitoring or managing the capacity of the remaining retailers, so as to facilitate SMEs having options to manage their electricity costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in light of five electricity retailers ceasing operations last year and many small and medium businesses (SMEs) having to shift back to SP Services' wholesale electricity plan, what support can be extended to these SMEs to provide more certainty to manage their business costs against very high increases in their monthly electricity charges, particularly those with average monthly electricity consumption of 4,000 kWh and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether he can provide an update on the Temporary Electricity Support Scheme (TRECS) since it was introduced in December 2021; (b) whether the TRECS will be extended beyond February 2022; and (c) whether EMA will consider working with electricity retailers to provide a 12-month fixed electricity plan for smaller business consumers, specifically SMEs with a monthly consumption between 4,000 and 20,000 kWh.

sections.label: Electricity retailers exiting market
sections.summary: Between October and December 2021, six electricity retailers exited and two terminated contracts, affecting about 9% of consumer accounts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Between October and December 2021, six electricity retailers exited the market and another two retailers prematurely terminated some of their customers' contracts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As a result, about 9% of all electricity consumer accounts were affected.

sections.label: TRECS and fixed price contracts
sections.summary: EMA worked with gencos and retailers to offer about 645 megawatts of TRECS and other fixed price plans, extending TRECS for March, April and May.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In response to requests for more such contracts, EMA worked with gencos and electricity retailers to offer about 645 megawatts of TRECS and other plans with significant fixed price components.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: At least 200 megawatts of the contracts are still available and we are extending TRECS for March, April and May.

sections.label: Question on extending TRECS
sections.summary: A question asks whether EMA can extend TRECS for another six to 12 months beyond May 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can EMA extend TRECS for another six to 12 months beyond May 2022, in view of the current economic and energy supply situation?

sections.label: TRECS extension for three months
sections.summary: The response states TRECS has now been extended for March, April and May.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As far as the extension of TRECS for another six months is concerned, we have now extended for March, April and May.

sections.label: TRECS extension and other assistance
sections.summary: TRECS is extended for March, April and May, and other assistance measures are being considered, with work to lower electricity costs through eligible contracts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, TRECS will be extended for March, April and through to May.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But other than TRECS as a scheme, we are also now working to see whether there are any other assistance measures that we can roll-out to help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, I hope that answers the Member's second point, For his first question, in terms of the assistance, we have worked with electricity retailers and gencos to lower the cost of buying electricity through eligible contracts to support those businesses that have been affected.

sections.label: Regulated tariff supply and gencos
sections.summary: SP buys regulated tariff electricity through long-term vesting contracts with gencos, and large consumers switching would require additional supply at higher prices or USEP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Electricity which is offered through the regulated tariff is purchased by SP through existing long-term vesting contracts with the gencos.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If we allow for large consumers to switch to the regulated tariffs, then this means that the SP Group will now have to contract for additional supply with gencos at higher prices and/or buy additional electricity supply from the SWEM at the prevailing Uniform Singapore Electric Price, or USEP.

sections.label: TRECS scheme for mid-sized consumers
sections.summary: To protect household consumers and small businesses, a new scheme, TRECS, is being negotiated for those in the four MWh to 20 MWh range.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This may not necessarily be fair to household consumers and small business owners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Hence, as a result of that, we wanted to make sure that we can segregate it and protect the existing consumers, of which many of them are your residents as well, by making sure that we move and negotiate for a new scheme, TRECS, to help those that are in the four MWh to 20 MWh range.
